lines: After the fire took the Kingdom of Vael, a mapmaker named Isolde walked into the ruin with a pot of ink and no one to sell a map to.
The mountains, being proud, had only changed their minds about where to stand.
She drew a bridge where a bridge had been, and the next morning the bridge was there, thin as a held breath, trembling over the dry bed of a stream.
She drew a village, a lamp in its window, a dog asleep on a step, and by evening the dog had shaken itself awake and begun to bark at her.
The ash, it turned out, was only listening.
It had been waiting for someone brave enough to say where things went.
On the last night she drew herself, small, at the edge of the page, and hesitated, her pen shaking above the empty paper.
Then, because every good map needs a place to come home to, she added a door.
